name: Reference configuration
description: Annex D reference sets every organization starts from. Starter profiles add to these; they never remove.

sets.title: Deliverable types
sets.description: D.1 — where the information came from; set at creation, never changes (§5.2).

sets.title: Document types
sets.description: Our own document types. What we produce carries a three-letter mnemonic (DWG, ITP); what a supplier delivers against a purchase order carries its family letter and a number (D101). Every type names its family, which is where the stamp rule is answered.

values.label: Weight and centre of gravity data
Spare parts list - two year operation
Special tools and lifting devices list

sets.title: Disciplines
sets.description: The disciplines a project works in. These are the general ones, meant for any kind of project — building, energy, water, thermal, industrial. A project type adds its own, and an organization is free to publish its own instead.

sets.title: Project codes
sets.description: C.2.3 — the scope within which numbers are unique. Replace with your projects.

sets.title: Sub-projects
sets.description: C.2.5 — publish your own breakdown (§4.4).

sets.title: Supplier / party codes
sets.description: C.2.4 — originator codes for external information (§3.3).

sets.title: Purchase orders
sets.description: Contract / PO codes (§4.4).

sets.title: Statuses
sets.description: D.5 — what a released revision may be used for; executionFlag permits physical execution (§7.8).

props.may: Awareness; planning around what is coming
props.mayNot: Any decision or work that depends on it being correct

props.may: A formal decision by the approving party
Building, installing, fabricating exactly what it shows
Recording what exists; operating, maintaining, modifying

sets.title: Review outcomes
sets.description: D.7 - the verdict on a submitted revision and what it does. Only the last step of a review route gives it, and a verdict that is final is the release approval. Earlier steps give advice, from Review advice.

values.label: For information only — no review needed

sets.title: Review advice
sets.description: What an advisory step says. Every step of a review route except the last gives advice: it is passed to the decider and never returns the document by itself. The last step gives a verdict, from Review outcomes. Nobody picks it: it follows from the comments that step left.

props.meaning: The step read the revision and wrote nothing.
The step left comments; none of them stops the release.
The step left a comment that stops the release until it is settled.

sets.title: Criticality
sets.description: D.8 — what consequence arises if the information is wrong (§5.6).

sets.title: Confidentiality
sets.description: C.4.6 — who may see it; default published (§5.7).

sets.title: Retention classes
sets.description: D.9 — how long, from which event (§13.1–13.3).

props.basis: Operation, maintenance or modification depends on it

sets.title: Reasons for issue
sets.description: §2.6 — what the recipient is expected to do, with periods (§11.12).

sets.title: Issue codes
sets.description: D.4 — organization codes mapped to the defined reasons (C.5.6).

sets.title: Phases
sets.description: C.4.4 — recorded against the revision (§5.5).

sets.title: Comment classifications
sets.description: D.10 - every comment says whether it stops release. A blocking comment must be settled before the revision is released; a comment that is not blocking is recorded and carried into the next revision.

props.meaning: Must be settled before the revision can be released.
Recorded, and answered in the next revision. It does not stop release.

sets.title: Type-to-field matrix
sets.description: C.3.3 — which conditional fields each deliverable type requires (§4.4).

sets.title: Reasons to send a revision back to a step
sets.description: Why a review route is rewound to an earlier step on the same revision. Every one of them is a fault in the route, not in the document.

props.meaning: What is under review is not the file that was meant to be reviewed.

values.label: The wrong people were on a step

props.meaning: A step was seated with people who should not have answered it, or missed people who should.
The route ran past a step that should have answered.

values.label: An answer was recorded in error

props.meaning: Somebody recorded a verdict on the wrong document, or against the wrong step.

sets.title: Contract roles
sets.description: What this organization is contracted to do on a project. It decides where approval sits and the distribution matrix the project starts from.

props.description: No contract role declared. The matrix applies as published, with no role-specific rows.

props.approval: With us. We approve our own engineering and our suppliers' data.
props.description: We hold design and execution. Vendor data comes to us; the client receives.

props.approval: With us, for engineering and for what the contractor submits.
props.description: We hold design and manage construction. The client keeps the commitment decisions, so there are two approval seats.

props.approval: Mostly outside us. The design office answers for its own content; the quality records stay ours.
props.description: We manage for the client and review contractor documents. Technical accuracy stays with whoever produced it.

props.approval: Checked by us, approved by the client.
props.description: We produce the design and check it internally. The approval that counts is the client's.

props.approval: With us. Everything comes to us.
props.description: We own the asset. Designers, contractors and suppliers all submit to us.

props.approval: With us for execution and quality; design stays with the designer.
props.description: We manage construction and hold no design.

sets.title: Document families
sets.description: The ten families every document type belongs to, keyed by the letter the supplier codes already carry. The family decides when an outside stamp is needed; the distribution matrix decides who gives it.

sets.title: Discipline groups
sets.description: The handful of groups every discipline falls in. A new sector adds its disciplines under an existing group, and anything that reads groups keeps working without knowing they exist.
